Hi Emma — thanks for the clear list, this is exactly what Legal/Security will want. I attached a short playbook and a BAA template you can share with procurement (see attachments). High level answers below and a recommended default approach we use with regulated customers.

Quick answers:
- Retention windows: per-tenant configurable. Defaults we recommend: 30 days (short), 90 days (standard), 365 days (extended). We can support custom windows up to multi-year (7 years) for regulated recordkeeping. You can set different windows for: raw ingestion (raw payload), derived artifacts (embeddings/indexes), request logs, and KV/prefix caches.
- Irreversible redaction vs pseudonymization: Redwood supports patterns for both but we strongly recommend redaction at the ingest boundary when legal/regulatory requirements mandate non-recoverability. Pseudonymization (tokenization) can improve model performance since it preserves structure, but it must be managed with strict key controls and your KMS policy.
- Field-level redaction before inference: we do not alter the model internals automatically, but offer a recommended architecture: an ingest preprocessor (customer-managed or our edge transform) that performs ML-assisted entity detection + deterministic regexes to either redact or pseudonymize fields before hitting the inference endpoint. We can provide an official set of entity detectors and pattern libraries for common PHI types (names, MRN, DOB, SSN), and integration instructions for DLP vendors.
- Deletion/attestation SLAs: Standard hosted flow: soft-delete propagation within 24 hours, permanent purge from active stores within 30 days of the retention window expiration. For customers requiring faster or auditable deletion we offer Dedicated or Private deployments: we can commit to a 7-day purge SLA and provide signed deletion attestation (PDF) that lists which buckets/objects were removed and timestamps. Attestation language is included in the BAA template.
- EU residency: Yes — Redwood can pin data to regions and provide Private deployments with customer-managed networking/keys in EU regions. Audit logs can be retained in-region per your retention policy.

Recommended baseline playbook (summary):
1) Ingest classification: classify each record as PII/PHI/None at the edge. Label fields that must be redacted vs pseudonymized.
2) Two-stream storage: keep raw payload in a short-term raw tier (configurable) + derived artifacts in a separate tier with its own retention.
3) Pre-inference transform: perform field-level redaction/pseudonymization at the preprocessor. If performance-sensitive, pseudonymize with KMS-backed tokens; otherwise permanently redact sensitive fields.
4) Cache policy: isolate KV and prefix caches per-tenant and set short live-times for PHI-containing contexts. Redwood can automatically evict cached tokens when a deletion event occurs.
5) Deletion attestation: upon request, produce a signed artifact that lists deleted object IDs, storage paths, and timestamps; include backup dek rotation notes where applicable.

Emma / Team — adding a technical note on tradeoffs and implementation patterns so Legal has visibility.

- Field-level redaction approaches:
  * Deterministic regex + canonicalization: fast, predictable for structured fields (MRN, DOB). Good for hard deletes.
  * ML entity detection (NER) + human review pipeline: useful for noisy clinical notes where PHI may be implicit. We recommend a staged approach: ML tag -> high-confidence automated redact -> low-confidence flagged for review.
  * Tokenization/pseudonymization: store a reversible map encrypted with your KMS (or Redwood-managed keys if you choose). Reversible flows require careful access control and audit logging; reversible tokens must themselves be rotated/expired to meet regulatory expectations.

- Caches & inference artifacts: note that local KV caches can contain decoded values if you keep plaintext in-memory for latency reasons. Our runtime supports per-tenant cache scoping and TTL-based eviction; we also provide a purge API that can evict an entire tenant cache namespace immediately. However, backups and async replicas may need additional coordination: for Dedicated/Private customers we support backup key rotation and a documented backup purge procedure.

- Implementation recommendation for MedForma (practical):
  1) Use edge preprocessor for redaction/pseudonymization.
  2) Keep raw payload in an encrypted short-term bucket (30 days), then run a scheduled irreversible purge for PHI fields while retaining minimal metadata for troubleshooting (non-PHI hashes only).
  3) Maintain an embedding/index store with independent retention (90 days default) and provide a deletion webhook that triggers index re-write to remove entries referencing deleted PHI.

Happy to provide a small proof-of-concept transformer that sits in front of the SDK. If Legal wants explicit sample contract language for the deletion attestation (timing + scope), we can propose: "Redwood will permanently purge specified customer data from active storage and accessible caches within 7 days of request and provide a signed attestation within 14 days confirming removal from active stores and scheduled backup deletion." We can tailor that for hosted vs private.
